CNN reports that Misao Okawa, the world's oldest person, died at age 117 in Osaka, Japan on Wednesday. Her family says she left behind three children, four grandchildren, and six great-grandchildren. She was born on March 5, 1898. Her family ran a kimono shop in Osaka. A nursing home employee said Okawa had a gentle personality and loved eating. Her favorite foods were sushi and udon noodles. She ate a lot of cake for her birthday last March 5.

As the Missouri National Guard got ready to go to Ferguson to stop riots, internal documents show they called the protesters "enemy forces" and "adversaries." The guard went there to help police, but many community leaders and civil rights activists said the police used too much force and made a bad situation worse. The protests started in August and continued until the end of the year.

Gunmen attacked the education ministry in Mogadishu, Somalia, on Tuesday. A suicide car bombing happened at the entrance, followed by gunmen entering the building. The attack killed at least 12 people and injured 16 others. The Islamist militant group Al-Shabaab claimed responsibility for the attack.

Gregory Margolin is 87 years old. When he was 16, he joined the Soviet Red Army to fight the Nazis in World War II. He did not tell people he was Jewish because he feared for his life. He fought hard, and his family had to flee to safety.

Many years later, Margolin found himself in another war. This year, in Ukraine, he became a sniper commander. He still wears his old military uniform with medals. His granddaughter Liora is amazed that he survived so much fighting.

More than 200 Nigerian schoolgirls disappeared exactly one year ago from their school in Chibok. The government and the world have failed to find them. We should all feel shame because young girls have had their lives destroyed by fanatics, and the world has forgotten about this tragedy very quickly.

In Norway, radio is changing. The country plans to stop using the old FM signal in two years. This will make Norway the first nation to do this completely. The government says people will not lose their radio shows. They will just need to use a digital signal instead. Officials say many of the country's 5 million people have already made this change. On the old FM signal, people can only find five stations. On the new digital signal, there are twenty times as many stations. The Culture Minister says half the country already listens using the digital signal.

Everyone loves a great comeback story, especially one that is very big. For over 100 years, the Brontosaurus was removed from science books. However, a new study suggests that the Brontosaurus is its own type of dinosaur, so it should have its own name.

In 1879, O.C. Marsh named the Brontosaurus after he found 25 crates of bones in Como Bluff, Wyoming. The Brontosaurus is similar to the Apatosaurus, but it is not as large. Marsh named the dinosaur "Brontosaurus," which means "thunder lizard."

CNN reports that Al Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula is offering a reward of 20 kilograms of gold—worth about $774,000—to anyone who kills or captures two specific leaders in Yemen. The group is targeting Abdelmalik Badruddin Al-Houthi, the leader of the rebels who took Yemen's capital, and former President Ali Abdullah Saleh. Al Qaeda refers to these two men as the "two heads of evil."

Before landing a gyrocopter on the Capitol lawn Wednesday, Doug Hughes wrote about his intentions and the reasons behind them on a website called thedemocracyclub.org. "The point of the flight is to spotlight corruption in DC and more importantly, to present the solution(s) to the institutional graft," the 61-year-old Florida postal carrier wrote in an online post titled "Your Pilot." "My flight is not a secret," the post says. "Before I took off, I sent an Email to info@barackobama.com. The letter is intended to persuade the guardians of the Capitol that I am not a threat and that shooting me down will be a bigger headache than letting me deliver these letters to Congress."

Bad news for Rio de Janeiro before the 2016 Olympics: many dead fish have been found in the Rodrigo de Freitas lagoon. With just over a year until the Games start, officials from the legislative assembly started an investigation into why the fish are dying. They are working with the State Environmental Institute and the Secretariat of State for the Environment to look into the problem in other lakes and bays as well.

Anthony Ray Hinton is 58 years old. For nearly 30 years, he lived on Alabama's death row in a small cell, about 5 by 7 feet. Until recently, he was in prison for a crime he did not commit. One week ago, his murder convictions were cleared, and he walked out of a jail in Birmingham. Hinton said he has to pinch himself to remember he is free. He is still getting used to being outside after so many years inside.

CNN reports that a poll about the UK election debate had no clear winner. Seven leaders took part: David Cameron (Conservatives), Ed Miliband (Labour), Nick Clegg (Liberal Democrats), Nigel Farage (UK Independence Party), Natalie Bennett (Green Party), Nicola Sturgeon (Scottish National Party), and Leanne Wood (Plaid Cymru).

Comres for ITV found that Cameron, Miliband, and Farage were tied for first place with 21% support each. Nicola Sturgeon was close behind with 20%. A separate poll by ICM for The Guardian gave Miliband 25 points, Cameron 24, Farage 19, and Sturgeon 17.

A New York judge has ruled that Facebook is an acceptable way to serve divorce papers. Ellanora Arthur Baidoo has been trying to divorce her husband for several years, but could not find him to give him the legal documents. She has been able to reach him by phone, but he told her he has no fixed address and no job.

It sounds like a science fiction movie. A person has a terrible accident and ends up in the hospital, brain dead and on life support. Doctors ask the family about organ donation, but instead of saving many lives, the family is asked to donate the whole body to save just one person. Perhaps a quadriplegic with a working mind but a failing body. As crazy as it sounds, Italian doctor Sergio Canavero says he is getting close to doing a head transplant. He calls this project HEAVEN, which stands for head anastomosis venture; anastomosis is surgically connecting two parts.

In 2013, an Atlanta hospital rejected Anthony Stokes for a heart transplant because of his "history of non-compliance." Two years later, Stokes died after leading police on a high-speed chase, shooting at an elderly woman, and crashing his car into a pole.

The sun had not risen over Garissa University College. Most students were still sleeping. A few had woken up to go to early morning Christian prayers. Suddenly, there was an explosion and gunfire at the school's front gates around 5:30 a.m. on Thursday. The attackers then moved across the campus. The Red Cross organization said they stopped at a girls' dormitory. At one point, the attackers burst into a room where Christians were gathered and took them hostage, according to lecturer Joel Ayora.

A white casket sat at the front of New Shiloh Baptist Church in West Baltimore. A gospel choir sang as a large crowd gathered to honor Freddie Gray. The 25-year-old died in police custody 15 days ago after he was arrested on a weapons charge. His death from a severe spinal injury sparked widespread outrage toward the Baltimore Police Department. Gray's death is the latest in a string of high-profile deaths involving African-Americans and law enforcement. Many demanded answers about what happened to Gray. His funeral drew civil rights leaders, politicians, and relatives of others who died in police custody.

I have been a chef since I was 14 years old. In 2007, my wife mentored a young girl who was forced to search through trash just to find food. This inspired me to start an organization called Food Policy Action and become active in politics regarding hunger and factory farms.

A major force behind this work has been "The Meatrix," a 2003 cartoon based on "The Matrix." It was produced by the GRACE Communications Foundation and showed the public health risks and environmental harms of factory farming.

Dan Swangard is a doctor who has seen many people die in hospitals. He has watched patients hooked to morphine and scared relatives standing by helplessly as death dragged on for weeks or months. In 2013, Swangard was diagnosed with a rare type of metastatic cancer. To remove the cancer, surgeons removed parts of his pancreas and liver, as well as his spleen and gallbladder. The surgery was successful, but Swangard, 48, knows there is a strong chance the disease will return.

CNN reports that Saudi special forces helped Yemeni fighters fight against the Houthis and their allies in Aden. The special forces were on the ground in noncombat roles, coordinating and guiding the battle. They also helped parachute in weapons and communications equipment. Following heavy Saudi airstrikes, Houthi rebels withdrew from the presidential palace and other key areas of Aden. This withdrawal marked a reversal of gains made the previous day, when Houthi forces seized the presidential palace.

A Detroit mother was arrested last month after police found two bodies in a freezer. Prosecutors charged Mitchelle Angela Blair with murder and torture in the deaths of her children, Stoni Ann Blair, 13, and Stephen Gage Berry, 9. Police say a bailiff found the bodies while doing a court-ordered eviction on March 24. The medical examiner says Stoni died from blunt trauma injuries and Stephen died from blunt trauma and thermal injuries.

Miami (CNN) - World heavyweight boxing champion Wladimir Klitschko has an important fight coming up on April 25 in New York. However, his thoughts are on the crisis in his home country, Ukraine. He spoke to CNN from his Miami training base. Klitschko said the situation in Ukraine has shocked and upset him. He explained that his country is suffering because of a war with Russia. He said Ukraine did not start the aggression, but Russia did.

Michael Keaton hosted "Saturday Night Live" for the third time. He made small jokes about his old roles in "Beetlejuice" and "Batman." Keaton first hosted the show in 1982. He said he has a son who is 31 and a girlfriend who is 28. Fans wanted him to act out his famous characters, but he only made a few jokes about them.

Just over a month ago, a jury found Kamron Taylor guilty of murder. Early Wednesday morning, Taylor escaped from an Illinois jail. He hid in his cell until a correctional officer walked by. Taylor then beat up the guard, put on the guard's uniform, and took the guard's keys. He used the keys to walk out of the jail and get into the guard's brown 2012 Chevrolet Equinox SUV. The 23-year-old Taylor was supposed to be sentenced in May. Police found the SUV around 8:30 a.m.

A New York City detective has been suspended after being accused of stealing $3,000 during a raid at a store. Police say the detective was caught on camera putting cash into a bag at the Yemen Deli and Grocery store in Brooklyn. The detectives had gone to the store to arrest two employees for selling loose cigarettes. The store manager noticed money was missing and checked the cameras, where he saw the detective take the money.

London (CNN) A safe deposit company in London was robbed over the holiday weekend. Thieves used heavy cutting equipment and ropes to break into the 60-year-old business. They spent possibly up to four days stealing gems and cash from the boxes. The thieves got away with hundreds of thousands of pounds worth of valuables. One former police official guessed the total value could be as high as 200 million pounds ($300 million).

As South Africa remembers the 1994 elections on April 27, new attacks against African migrants have sparked anger online. People are using the hashtag #WeAreAfrica to demand action, fearing that these attacks show the country's dream of a fair, equal society has failed.

In 1989, Ayatollah Khomeini agreed to a ceasefire to stop the eight-year war with Iraq. The war had helped define his Islamic Republic government, which he had started one year before Saddam Hussein invaded Iran. Khomeini encouraged the nation to fight, even though Saddam wanted to end the war sooner. He kept the conflict on for eight years, which helped build the Islamic Republic. However, when the war ended, the economy was collapsed, and his supporters had disappeared.

The United States has benefited greatly from being a leader in space travel. U.S. access to space has helped the country's national security, defense, and economy. The military relies on space-based technology, like intelligence, GPS, and communications satellites, to handle current and future threats. However, the U.S. is too dependent on Russian technology to meet its national security needs.

On the one-year anniversary of the schoolgirls' abduction in Nigeria, Malala Yousafzai wrote an open letter to the victims. The 17-year-old Nobel Peace Prize winner, who survived a Taliban attack in Pakistan for going to school, asked the Nigerian government and the international community to do more to rescue the girls. She wrote that, like the kidnapped girls, she was a target of militants who did not want girls to go to school. Nigeria recently held an election.

CNN reports that South African soldiers were sent out on Tuesday evening to help stop deadly attacks against foreigners. Their first stop was the Johannesburg area of Jeppestown, where violence broke out on Friday. The military helped police take control of a hostel in Jeppestown. Defense Minister Nosiviwe Mapisa-Nqakula said the government will send an unknown number of soldiers to places where police are struggling to stop the attacks.

Eight Iranian border guards were killed in a fight with militants near the border with Pakistan. Three of the militants were also killed. The fight happened in the town of Negur in southeastern Iran. The militants came into Iran from Pakistan. Iranian officials have asked Pakistani authorities to catch the surviving militants.

TripAdvisor named Providenciales in the Turks and Caicos the world's best island. The island moved up one spot from last year to take the top spot, pushing Ambergris Caye out of first place. Ambergris Caye had held the number one spot for two years in a row, but it fell out of the top ten completely this year. TripAdvisor spokeswoman Julie Cassetina said it is hard to say why the change, as winners change from year to year based on traveler feedback.

At the Star Wars Celebration fan festival in Anaheim, California, details about the 2016 movie "Rogue One" were shared. Director Gareth Edwards showed an early teaser and confirmed the film will take place between "Episode III: Revenge of the Sith" and "Episode IV: A New Hope." The story follows a group of rebels on a dangerous mission to steal the plans for the Death Star. Felicity Jones stars as a rebel soldier in this anthology film.

Tehran, Iran (CNN) -- A Persian proverb says a good year depends on its spring. For many Iranians, the decision by Tehran and six world powers to keep nuclear talks going is a sign that the Persian New Year, which started on March 21, will be a great one. Although some hardliners may complain the preliminary agreement is not enough, many people see this as excellent progress.

Ferguson, Missouri (CNN) Two African-American candidates, Ella Jones and Wesley Bell, won seats on the Ferguson City Council on Tuesday. This means three of the six council members are now black.

The election took place on Tuesday. It was the first city election since a white police officer shot and killed an unarmed black teenager named Michael Brown last August.

Voters went to the polls at 6 a.m. The weather was bad, with rain and warnings of flash floods. Usually, very few people vote in these local elections. But today, more people came out to vote.

An Israeli man was killed and a woman was hurt when a 37-year-old Arab driver from East Jerusalem hit them at a bus stop in French Hill, Jerusalem. Police say it looks like a terror attack. The driver has been arrested and is being investigated by the General Security Services. One of the victims, Shalom Yohai Cherki, 26, died at the hospital. The other victim, a 20-year-old woman, is in serious condition.

A collection of art owned by the late actress Lauren Bacall was sold in New York on March 31. The collection included works by famous 20th-century artists. It had been shown in Hong Kong, Paris, London, and Los Angeles before the sale. Bacall died in 2014 at age 89. She became famous in 1944 with the film "To Have And Have Not," and she met her husband, Humphrey Bogart, at that time. George Clooney honored her at the 2015 Golden Globes.

Kiev, Ukraine (CNN)
The question on people's minds in Kiev right now is: Who is killing allies of Ukraine's ousted President Viktor Yanukovych?

The idea that this might be happening is not new. But it came back into the spotlight this week after two high-profile shootings happened in the Ukrainian capital. One of the victims was Oleg Kalashnikov, a former member of parliament with ties to Yanukovych. He was shot and killed Wednesday evening near his apartment. The other victim was a Ukrainian journalist known for his pro-Russian views.

CNN) Chile will soon recognize civil unions for same-sex couples. President Michelle Bachelet signed a new law on Monday that allows these unions. She said this is a step to end the difference between gay and straight couples. The law will start in six months. It gives legal rights to couples living together, whether they are two people of the same sex or a man and a woman. The government says about 2 million people will benefit from this change.

The next time you fly to Florida to visit Grandma, or take the kids to see the mouse or South Beach, look out the window before you land. The Everglades look like a swampy wasteland full of dangerous things: snakes, scorpions, rats, roaches, gators, and mosquitoes. A researcher once caught 365,000 bloodthirsty bugs in a single trap in just one night. This place shows the folly of man and the cost of redemption.

CNN reports that ISIS militants took control of Yarmouk, a Palestinian refugee camp near Damascus, after defeating other militia groups there. The residents were besieged and bombed by Syrian forces for over two years. One resident told CNN that ISIS fighters "slaughtered them in the streets," killing three people in front of others. The Islamic State now controls almost all the camp.

China's government has long blocked its citizens from reading Western news websites using a "Great Firewall." Now, a new study says they have developed a "Great Cannon." This new tool allows them to attack servers outside of China, including in the United States. The study's authors warn that this visible attack could cause international anger, and Beijing may have expected this reaction.

A German official said investigators still do not know why co-pilot Andreas Lubitz crashed Germanwings Flight 9525. However, the official said Lubitz had suicidal thoughts before he became a pilot. Investigators have not found any letters or conversations where Lubitz explained his reasons. Medical records show he was suicidal and received therapy before he ever got his pilot's license.

The leader of Yemen's Houthi rebels said on Sunday that his group will not give up. This came after a top Saudi military official said weeks of airstrikes had weakened the Shiite group.

In a televised speech, rebel leader Abdul-Malik al-Houthi said his fighters will not leave the main cities or the government institutions. He added that anyone hoping the group will surrender is " dreaming."

His comments came after more than three weeks of Saudi-led coalition bombings. The airstrikes are aimed at pushing back the Houthis, who surged into the capital of Sanaa in January and ousted President Abdu Rabu Mansour Hadi from power.

On April 19, 1995, Timothy McVeigh exploded a large truck bomb in front of the Murrah Federal Building in Oklahoma City. The explosion killed 168 people and injured hundreds of others. It remains the deadliest act of domestic terrorism in United States history. The attack shocked the nation because it was the first time American citizens had targeted their own government with such deadly force.

If you care deeply about something, you might protest, make a sign, or join a demonstration. How long can you keep going, even if people ignore you and do nothing?

More than 200 Nigerian girls were kidnapped from their school by Boko Haram militants a year ago. Millions of people around the world joined a social media campaign to ask for their safe return. Charles Alasholuyi was one of those people, along with celebrities and world leaders. They voiced their anger using the hashtag #BringBackOurGirls, which became one of the top Twitter hashtags of 2014. It was used in more than four million tweets.

However, as weeks turned into months, the missing girls still had not been found. The attention on the campaign faded

Barney Frank, a retired congressman, recently spoke in Chicago. He entertained a sold-out crowd by talking about his 45 years in public service. Frank is well-known for being the first member of Congress to marry someone of the same-sex while in office. He also had strong words for politicians who hide their sexuality while voting against LGBT rights. When asked about a California ballot proposal that would legalize killing gay people, Frank said he was not aware of the measure but told the young man not to worry about " crazy people. "

CNN reports that a brutal attack on Garissa University College in Kenya left about 150 people dead, including students, and dozens more wounded. Gunmen attacked the campus early Thursday while morning prayers were happening, shooting randomly and taking hostages before being killed by security forces. Officials say Al-Shabaab militants claimed responsibility. This attack comes months after Al-Shabaab killed non-Muslim workers in a Kenyan quarry. The group has been behind many attacks in the area and has recruited some Americans, especially from the Somali-American community in Minnesota.

Students at the University of Cape Town in South Africa have successfully removed a statue of Cecil Rhodes. The students had protested for weeks, saying the statue honored a man whose legacy was based on racism. Using the hashtag #RhodesMustFall, they demanded the statue come down. After four weeks, the university removed the statue following permission from the heritage authority. The university stated the removal was to ensure the statue's safety while decisions about its future are made.

Syria is a very dangerous place. A group that opposes the government says many people have died there. Since the civil war started, 310,000 people have been killed. One year ago, the number was 162,402. Two years ago, the United Nations said 70,000 people had died.

The United Nations says that more than half of all Syrians are very poor. They need help to survive because food rations have been cut due to a lack of donations.

CNN reports that Ailina Tsarnaeva was not shy when threatening a woman she considered a rival. Prosecutors say she called the woman and threatened to "put a bomb where you live" if she stopped looking for her man. Because of who she is, prosecutors charged her with aggravated harassment. Tsarnaeva, the sister of Dzhokhar and Tamerlan Tsarnaev, denies the charge.

A Gaza police official said on Thursday that police took a door with a drawing by the artist Banksy. The door's owner, Rabea Darduna, said he sold the door for only $175 because he did not know it was valuable. When Darduna's home was destroyed last summer, he says he felt he had nothing left but a doorway and a door. Police are keeping the door until a court date is decided.

A Saudi-led coalition is attacking Houthi rebels in Yemen. Five days after the first airstrikes, the coalition has destroyed the rebels' air defense systems and most of their air bases. Saudi Arabia's navy now controls all Yemeni ports, only allowing in closely watched medical supplies. Locals are fleeing the fighting, and the death toll is rising, including many civilians.

Holland manager Guus Hiddink was very angry at his own fans for booing Spain's Andres Iniesta during the game on Tuesday. Spain played with a backup team, and Iniesta came into the game in the 76th minute. The home crowd jeered and booed him. Despite this, Stefan de Vrij and Davy Klaassen scored goals in the first half, giving Holland a 2-0 win. Hiddink called the fans' behavior a 'disgrace'.

Scotland will find out on May 21 if their game against Georgia in September will be played without fans. UEFA, European football's governing body, has started an investigation into the Georgian Football Federation. This follows two separate incidents where fans ran onto the field during Georgia's 2-0 loss to Germany in Tbilisi on Sunday. UEFA is also looking into other charges, including fans setting off fireworks and safety problems at the stadium, like blocked stairs and locked gates.

Football agents were unsure about their future on Wednesday while waiting for new rules to be announced. Starting April 1st, anyone can become a football agent by paying a £500 fee for the first year. The FA will then charge £250 every year after that. Agents who already have a license are exempt from these new rules. The FA was supposed to have a website ready by 1pm for agents to sign up, but it was not ready yet. Mel Stein believes these new rules will cause chaos. These new guidelines started after FIFA decided to stop managing agents.

CSKA Sofia's Latvian goalkeeper Maksims Uvarenko has not been paid for three months. He has had to ask his parents to send him money to pay his rent. He has been at the club since January on an 18-month contract. Despite the financial problems, he has been impressed by the passionate support of the fans. He told local media that the lack of money is the biggest problem he has faced at the club.

David Moore, 25, got very angry on the road right after he left his house. He found himself stuck in heavy traffic right next to Rafal Cegielka, 45, who was picking up his child from school. Moore then punched the father and smashed his car with a hockey stick while young children watched, because he was having a "bad day" and saw red.

Spain lost 2-0 to Holland on Tuesday. This defeat reminded coach Vicente del Bosque and his team of their bad performance at the 2014 World Cup. Gerard Pique, a player on the team, said the coach was not too worried about losing three friendly games in a row.

Holland beat Spain 5-1 in the group stage of last year's World Cup in Brazil. That game ended Spain's six-year time as the best team in the world. On Tuesday, Holland scored two early goals at the Amsterdam Arena. Even though Spain pressed them hard in the second half, Holland held on to win 2-0.

A New York City mother and her daughter have fled to Germany during a custody battle, police say. Ulrike Berger, 44, is not allowed to leave the country with her seven-year-old daughter, Kaia. However, on March 22, the pair boarded a plane to Europe.

Police are searching for Ulrike Berger and her daughter. It is believed they flew from New York to Germany on March 22, breaking a court order. Police say the pair were last seen at Berger's home in Boerun Hill, Brooklyn, at 10:00 AM on March 21, when Kaia's father dropped her off for a visit.

A huge fire ripped through dry heathland near the south coast. The fire looked like something from a disaster movie. It destroyed an area the size of 100 football pitches. This happened after days of storms hit Britain, knocking down trees and shutting roads. However, a 70-hectare area of Dorset was extremely dry because much of it is on a hillside, and rain had run off down the slope. Fire investigators confirmed the fire was started on purpose. They found that three separate areas of heath— measuring half a hectare, one hectare, and 70 hectares— were destroyed.

Last night, emergency services were very busy. They received about 600 calls every hour because people were drinking heavily to celebrate the New Year. Paramedics were extremely busy, and in Cambridge, they set up a field hospital to help drunk partygoers.

The London Ambulance Service said at the busiest time, they were handling over 600 calls per hour. This was more than three times the normal amount of calls.

In Manchester, a man collapsed on the pavement next to an ambulance while two revellers walked by eating food. In another part of Manchester, a man was slumped over in a doorway while two women walked by celebrating the New Year.

Liverpool goalkeeper Simon Mignolet said his mental strength helped him recover after being dropped in December. He was dropped indefinitely by manager Brendan Rodgers because of poor form, but he returned quickly after Brad Jones got hurt. Mignolet told how he tried to stay positive despite the disappointment.

Giant hailstones the size of plums fell over the South on Tuesday. Residents went outside to record the strange weather. A Twitter user named Arke USA from Bryant, Arkansas, filmed the ice balls hitting his backyard and pool. The video shows the hailstones falling quickly and cracking when they hit the ground. Even though it was about 80 degrees outside, the hail stayed on the patio for a long time. In seconds, the patio was covered in white pellets.

A replica pirate ship called the Liana's Ransom ran into trouble about 30 miles off the coast of Maine. The ship's engines failed around 12:35 p.m. on Monday, and its sails got tangled around the mast. Because of the rough seas, the crew had to abandon the ship. The U.S. Coast Guard rescued nine crew members using their life boats. The ship was left adrift in the ocean.

Amazing pictures have emerged of blue fluorescent algae lighting up Australia's east coast. The images were taken in Jervis Bay, on the south coast of NSW, as the neon glow illuminated one of Australia's popular beaches. Photographer Andy Hutchinson described the sight as a 'beautiful supernatural scene' caused by millions of plankton omitting light. A similar display was shown in Sydney's Manly Beach back in August 2014 where an oceanography expert told Daily Mail Australia there was no need to be concerned about the algae.

A 17-year-old boy named Rahul Kumar climbed over a fence into a lion enclosure at a zoo in Ahmedabad, India. He was drunk and began running toward the animals, shouting that he would kill them. Zoo security had to rescue him. Mr. Kumar later explained that he was intoxicated and thought he could fight the lions.

A 12-year-old boy fell out of a five-story window and survived by landing on a car parked below. His father said the boy was probably sleepwalking when he fell. The accident happened last Saturday in Nanchang, China. A hotel worker across the road heard a loud noise at midnight and thought it was a car crash.

Red Wings player Drew Miller is happy to be back on the ice just one day after he got cut. He says he feels very lucky the skate did not hit his eye. Miller was skating with a full face mask. He had a bad cut on his face that needed 50 to 60 stitches to close. He got the cut from another player. He has a scar across his eye, but he did not lose eyesight.

Filipe Luis says he wants to stay at Chelsea until his contract ends, even though Atletico Madrid wants to sign him back in the summer. He signed a three-year deal last July, but has had trouble playing at his best at Stamford Bridge. Atletico hope this gives them an advantage, but Luis said he is happy at Chelsea and wants to finish his contract there.

A 20-year-old fan ran onto the pitch during a soccer game and did flips. He was banned from soccer for three years because of it.

The fan, Charlie Sumner, ran onto the field at Reading's stadium during a cup game last month. He did four front flips before stewards stopped him. He said it was his first game ever, and he thought it was a "brilliant experience."

A video shows a van carrying football fans swerving around a corner in Salé, Morocco. About half a dozen people were sitting on the roof of the vehicle. As the van moved at high speed, it toppled onto one side, sending the people riding on top flying. The footage was taken from a car following the van.

England have been drawn in Group D with the Republic of Ireland, Holland, and Italy at the UEFA Under 17 European Championships in Bulgaria in May.

John Peacock's Young Lions are the defending champions after winning last year's final on penalties in Malta. To progress to the quarter-finals, England must overcome Holland again, as the tournament has been expanded from eight to 16 teams for the first time.

Danny Collinge scored his first England goal in qualifying.

An angry elephant tried to spray a buffalo bull with water because the bull got too close. The elephant was relaxing in South Africa's Kruger National Park with its family by a small pool. In a video, the elephant squirted water from its trunk at the bull, but missed. The bull then drank from the pool while the elephant's young calf stayed close for safety.

Michael Thorpe, a former pub landlord, has had his conviction overturned after an eight-year legal battle. He was found guilty in 2006 of showing Premier League football matches on foreign TV channels at his pub in Plymouth. Mr. Thorpe, 55, says the fight to clear his name cost him heavily, resulting in the loss of his pub.

The Irish Football Association is worried that damage at its Windsor Park home in Belfast might stop the June game against Romania. Cracks appeared in the West Stand on Tuesday morning, and engineers checked the area. The Irish FA learned about the damage on Tuesday. O night, Windsor Park's West Stand got damaged.

A 20-year-old football fan has been banned for three years after running onto the pitch and doing somersaults during his first game at Reading's stadium.

Charlie Sumner ran onto the field during an FA Cup match last month. While his team was winning 3-0, he did four front flips. He was caught and tackled by security stewards.

A man driving a BMW car with five children inside was arrested today. He is suspected of hitting and killing Hina Shamim, a 21-year-old student, as she walked to the library near Kingston University in London. Hina died last night, just weeks before her 22nd birthday. Her friends placed flowers at the scene. They said Hina, who was from Peterborough and nicknamed "Hyena," was a much-loved and charming young woman.

A mother and her teenage daughter were arrested after a video of them fighting with a student at a high school was posted online. The incident happened at Langham Creek High School in Houston on Tuesday. The mother was angry because she said the student had been bullying her daughter. In the video, the mother is seen wearing a black top on the right side, and the student she is fighting is wearing white in the center.

Stoke chief executive Tony Scholes wants to keep goalkeeper Asmir Begovic. Begovic has one year left on his contract and has been linked with other clubs. Scholes believes Stoke can meet the 27-year-old's goals. He said Begovic is a great goalkeeper and they want to keep him at the club.

A bus driver in Auckland, New Zealand was filmed reading a newspaper while driving. A passenger took a video of the driver flicking through the paper as the bus moved. The passenger sent the video to the bus company, Ritchies Coachlines, along with a complaint. The company's boss, Andrew Ritchie, said he was embarrassed by the driver's actions and called him a "complete idiot."

West Ham manager Sam Allardyce says Winston Reid will play on Saturday against Leicester City. Reid hurt his hamstring in a game against Chelsea on March 4, but he is now fit after training during the break. However, Enner Valencia cannot play. Valencia missed the last two games because of a toe injury he got at home in mid-Mrech, but Allardyce says he is not ready yet.

Five days before their wedding last May, a car crash killed Brittany Huber and left her fiancé, John Redman, fighting for his life. Doctors told Redman he would likely spend the rest of his life in a nursing home, confined to a wheelchair. However, Redman recovered against all odds. On March 24, the 25-year-old college basketball coach helped lead his team to a championship title.

Lucas (left) and Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard before Sunday's All-Star charity game at Anfield.

Liverpool midfielder Lucas Leiva is trying to get back to his best form after recovering from injury. He started 16 games in 19 matches from late November, which helped the team win more. However, a groin injury in February's Merseyside derby kept him out for 10 games.

He was an unused substitute in a loss to Manchester United before the international break, but played the full 90 minutes in Sunday's All-Star game.

Japanese photographer Yûki Aoyama takes pictures of fathers jumping into the air while their daughters smile at the camera. He made this series because he was bored with normal portraits. The photos are from his new book, which is called "Daughter and Salary Man."

Police are looking for a man between 50 and 60 years old. He is suspected of robbing a bank in broad daylight and running away with £3,000 in cash.

The robbery happened at 12:30pm at a Lloyds Bank branch in Fairwater, Cardiff. Police have released CCTV images of the suspect. He is between 5ft 9in and 6ft tall and was wearing black clothing.

The suspect is a white man with greying black hair and glasses. Police say no one was hurt during the robbery and they are confident the public can identify him.

The Court of Arbitration for Sport has allowed Morocco to compete in the next two African Cup of Nations tournaments. Morocco was originally banned from the 2017 and 2019 tournaments and fined $1 million by the Confederation of African Football after pulling out due to the Ebola epidemic. The CAF had also demanded an additional $9 million in compensation. Now that the ban is lifted, Morocco can compete in the upcoming tournaments.

Tom Boyd thinks Jason Denayer has done such a good job on loan at Celtic that he is ready to play for Manchester City next season. This would stop Celtic from keeping him for another year, but Boyd thinks it is still a good thing because it might encourage other young players to join Celtic in the future. Jason Denayer, a 19-year-old defender, has played well for Celtic this season. He recently got his first call to the Belgium national team for a Euro 2016 qualifying game against Cyprus.

Andros Townsend scored a great goal for England, silencing people who had criticized him. The 23-year-old had a difficult season but played well in England's 1-1 friendly match against Italy in Turin. Manager Roy Hodgson kept faith in Townsend, who repaid that trust with an excellent goal. He celebrated the goal with his Tottenham teammates Ryan Mason and Kyle Walker.

Chinese company Dalian Wanda Group has officially bought 20% of the Spanish soccer team Atletico Madrid. The deal was finalized on Tuesday after the legal team signed the papers. They bought 726,707 shares for 45 million euros (about 32.8 million pounds). The purchase was announced in January, but it took two meetings to make it official. Wanda Group chairman Wang Jianlin wants to help Atletico grow its brand in Asia. Atletico Madrid manager Diego Simeone talks to the media.

Antonio Conte returned to Turin for Italy's 1-1 draw against England. He said the visit brought him "very fond memories," even though reports said he received death threats before the game.

Conte became Italy's manager in August, replacing Cesare Prandelli after Italy was eliminated from the World Cup group stage. His first seven months in charge have been difficult. Italy needed a late goal from Eder to rescue a 2-2 draw against Bulgaria last Saturday. Reports say Conte received death threats from Juventus fans after Claudio Marchisio suffered a knee injury on the eve of the Euro 2016 qualifier.

Ian Murray thinks that Hibernian can catch Rangers for second place in the Championship. His team, Dumbarton, have played both Rangers and Hibs already this season and will play them again before the season ends. While Rangers are doing well at the moment, Murray believes they will struggle to keep up their current pace, and that Hibs will eventually take second place.

Liverpool goalkeeper Simon Mignolet returned to England after playing for Belgium in Euro 2016 qualifying matches. Although he was in the match-day squad for the games against Cyprus and Israel, he did not play. Chelsea's Thibaut Courtois was chosen as the starter instead. Mignolet posted photos of himself posing in a pilot's cockpit on his Facebook page on Wednesday.

A large rural estate is for sale at £6 million. It is near Bridgnorth, Shropshire, and covers 200 acres of land. The property includes a Grade II-listed manor house built in 1814, five cottages, a swimming pool, tennis court, stables, and its own cricket green. The main house, Chyknell Hall, has 11 bedrooms and has only been sold twice before. Its secluded location offers complete privacy, which may attract high-profile buyers.

Two college campus police officers in Dallas have been placed on leave after video showed them harassing a group of students and hitting one of them. The incident happened at El Centro College last Wednesday. Student Charles Adams recorded the event on his phone while he was smoking a cigarette outside the campus. The officers approached a group of high school students who were waiting for a bus.

Gary Locke has been made the permanent manager of Kilmarnock. He signed a three-year contract after doing the job temporarily since February. The 39-year-old, who has only lost once in seven games, will speak to the media on Friday.

This weekend, one of the biggest games on the German football calendar takes place. Borussia Dortmund and Bayern Munich have won the last five league titles between them, and Bayern are expected to keep winning this season.

Usually, this game is called "Der Klassiker." However, this time the two teams are not in the same position in the league table. Bayern is leading, while Dortmund is lower down the list. There is a gap of nine points between them. Even though the points are different, the importance of the match is the same as usual.

Jurgen Klop celebrated with his Borussia Dortmund players after they beat Hannover.

A 14-year-old girl was left stuck at London Stansted airport after easyJet refused to let her fly home to Spain. Deva Joseph was upset because she was only allowed one small bag, but she had two. She offered to pay to check the second bag, but the airline only accepted credit cards. She does not have a credit card, so she was not allowed to board the plane.

Gordon Robson, 26, punched 45-year-old John Potts in the back of the head outside a sports bar. The hit was so hard it made a loud cracking sound, and Mr. Potts fell down and died. Robson, who has a history of violent behavior, was sentenced to three and a half years in prison for the attack that happened after his grandfather's funeral.

Ellen White scored a free kick against her old team, Arsenal. She hit the ball while her teammates Laura Bassett and Alex Greenwood almost crashed into each other. This happened in the 26th minute of the game.

These are the amazing scenes as high school girls in China are put through their paces with military-style dagger drills. Each of the girls shout the words 'kill, stab, slash and jab' as they perform each of the eight set movements involved in the high-intensity knife-fighting session. According to the People's Daily Online, the girls of the 27th March Huizhou Integrated High School are being trained by former special forces soldier Inspector Tan. The 68 girls involved in the training are all aged between 16 and 18, however in a concession to safety, the knives are not real. School official Huang Anruo said: 'The daggers are fake.'

We spend about a third of our lives sleeping. However, many people do not realize what their mind and body need during these resting hours to feel refreshed. According to the Sleep Health Foundation, 30 percent of Australians complain about a lack of sleep every day. Professor David Hillman says that lost sleep must be "paid back" to function well during the week. On average, adults need about eight hours of sleep per night, ranging between seven and nine hours.

A video posted on Facebook shows a heated argument between neighbours in a Perth suburb that turned violent. In the clip, an angry woman yracist slurs and a metal crowbar at a group of men who appear to be of African descent. The men fight back, and a scuffle breaks out. The woman can be heard shouting, "I don't deal with monkeys. Go on now you f*****g monkeys."

Everyone is watching Valencia's 19-year-old left back Jose Luis Gaya. Manchester City, Arsenal, and Chelsea want to sign him this summer. Real Madrid also wants to keep him.

Sportsmail writer Pete Jenson looks at the Spain under-21 defender. English clubs want him because his buy-out clause is only £13.5 million. For comparison, Luke Shaw, a player of a similar age and potential, cost £27 million. Because the price is so much lower, it would be a good deal to sign him. However, there might be questions about whether he is suited to the Premier League.

Jose Luis Gaya played for Valencia in a La Liga match against Sevilla earlier this season.

Police in Oregon are asking the public for help finding a man on a green motorcycle. He saved two teenagers after a 59-year-old man named Edward West allegedly pulled a gun on them. The motorcyclist used his helmet to knock the gun out of West's hands, letting the teens run away.

Tim Sherwood has asked Ron Vlaar to prove himself again now that he is fit. Sherwood wants the defender to help Aston Villa avoid relegation. Vlaar was an important player for Holland in the World Cup last year, even though he missed a penalty in a shoot-out against Argentina. He is returning to the team for their match at Old Trafford on Saturday.

Tim Sherwood says he is not worried about a possible takeover of Aston Villa. He plans to stay and build a new team for next season, but only if the team stays in the league. Owner Randy Lerner is in talks to sell the club. However, Sherwood is focused on keeping Villa safe first, before making big changes in the summer.

Christian Benteke celebrates scoring as Aston Villa thrash Sunderland last month.

Celtic hoped to keep Jason Denyer on loan from Manchester City next season. However, Manchester City's manager, Manuel Pellegrini, says his young players are not yet good enough to join the first team. This means Denyer might have to return to Manchester City instead of staying at Celtic.

Southampton manager Ronald Koeman is waiting for a more accurate return date for Fraser Forster before deciding whether to sign a new goalkeeper this summer. Forster injured his knee during Southampton's 2-0 win over Burnley two weeks ago, and his recovery is expected to take between four and twelve months. Koeman does not want to give a specific timeline for Forster's return and considers Kelvin Davis capable of covering for him, although he may be forced to bring in a new keeper if Forster is sidelong.

Rotherham boss Steve Evans was angry on the sidelines after his team were denied a penalty in their narrow Championship defeat by Birmingham. Birmingham led 2-0 at halty through goals by Robert Tesche and Clayton Donaldson. Matt Derbyshire pulled one back for Rotherham. However, referee Dean Whitestone waved away appeals for a penalty after Rob Kiernan clumsily handled Matt Derbyshire in the box. Rotherham are fourth from the bottom.

The worry about Virgil van Dijk is clear. Holland’s national team has already let in more goals in five Euro 2016 qualifying games than they gave up during the whole qualifying campaign for the last World Cup. Even though, Guus Hiddink never calls or writes. The Celtic defender made it into two squads last year. However, one step forward is usually followed by two steps back. When the Dutch were drawing 1-1 with Turkey the other night, he was sunning himself in the Arabian Gulf and bumping into club-mates instead. Virgil van Dijk has been in fine form for Celtic but wasn't rewarded with a call-up to the Holland national team.

Celtic have complained to the Scottish Football Association (SFA) about ticket prices for their Scottish Cup semi-final against Inverness at Hampden this month.

The SFA set the prices at £23 for the North and South stands, and £15 for adults or £5 for concessions in the East Stand. The match is scheduled for 12.15pm on Sunday, April 18.

Rangers interim chairman Paul Murray said on Thursday night that previous boardroom leaders were entirely to blame for the club being removed from the stock exchange. The team will have to leave the Alternative Investment Market (AIM) because they could not find a new nominated advisor to follow the rules. Murray says this change will not affect the new board's future plans or any planned investments.

Wayne Rooney and his England teammates were upset by their poor start against Italy on Tuesday. It was their first meeting in nine months, since the World Cup. England had won seven games in a row, but they struggled early. Italy took the lead with a header. The game finished 1-1. Rooney said the team was unhappy with how they played in the first half.

Dundee United's two main fan groups are angry about how the club's leaders are doing. They are shocked that 25% of the money made from selling four players went to unknown middlemen. The groups also disagree with how much the chairman has invested in the team. The board says the fans are wrong because the team has been winning on the field.

Gary Locke will be announced as Kilmarnock's permanent manager on Friday. He got the job eight weeks after being asked to lead the team until the end of the season. The club will give him a three-year contract. Locke, 39, thanked the players for helping him impress new chairman Jim Mann after he took the job on a temporary basis in February.

Chinese parents love raising children who are very talented. Some children start school at age 10, and some start dancing at age four. Now, a new basketball star is becoming popular. A video is going viral in China. It shows a small boy, who is only five years old, doing amazing basketball tricks. The boy's name is Mai Zizhuo. He has been playing basketball since he was two and a half. The video starts with the boy scoring many points. Then, he runs around while dribbling two basketballs.

Bayern Munich will miss David Alaba for the end of the season. The 22-year-old defender hurt his knee while playing for Austria against Bosnia on Tuesday. Doctors say he is out for about seven weeks. This is a tough injury for Alaba, who was already out for three months earlier this season with a similar knee problem. He said he is disappointed but wants to be fit for the end of the season.

Hull KR have signed experienced Australian forward Dane Tilse to replace the injured Michael Weyman and Ryan Bailey. The 6ft 7in, 17st-plus Tilse has agreed to a two-and-a-half-year deal and will join the team as soon as paperwork is complete. At 30 years old with 200 games in Australia, Tilse will link up with teammate Terry Campese and act as a direct replacement for Weyman, who retired last month due to injury.

Livingston boss Mark Burchill thinks Darren Cole will play in Sunday's final, even though Cole's cousin Shaun died last week. Shaun, 22, was found dead in Miami after a hit-and-run accident. He was a soldier who had been on holiday in Florida. Burchill is hopeful Cole will play on Sunday.

Alan Smith has denied claims that Liverpool fans attacked the ambulance he was in after he was injured during a Manchester United vs. Liverpool match nine years ago.
